transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess work’s been getting messy. I’m an electrician, and lately I can’t stay on one estimate or code form. Like, a tool noise, a text, or some idea about my workshop pulls me off, and then I come back and things are mixed up. That’s kind of what finally made me come in.
Did you have this same kind of trouble focusing when you were a child?
I don’t really know. I mean, school wasn’t my favorite, but I can’t say I remember it being like this. Not clearly, anyway.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energized and needed much less sleep than usual?

Yeah… I guess so. For the last few months I’ve been sleeping maybe three or four hours, and then I’m up before dawn like I’m fine. I’ll start pricing materials or answering emails, sketching out some system… it doesn’t really feel like I missed sleep.
During those times when you only sleep three or four hours, do you feel unusually cheerful or high?

Yeah… kind of. I get really pumped up, like I’m talking like our little shop’s about to be the main solar outfit in town. But it’s not always cheerful. If my wife or one of the apprentices questions it, I can get… pretty sharp, over nothing.
When you’re sleeping only three or four hours and feel pumped up, do you take on a lot more projects or work than usual?

Yeah. I mean… I’ve been doing a lot. Going from job sites to bids, then back to the workshop messing with test panels. I’ll start some new home-automation thing before I’ve even finished the last one. Sitting still just feels like… wasting time.
During these pumped-up periods, have you spent much more money than usual or made big purchases you normally wouldn’t?
I don’t know… not really big purchases, I don’t think. Maybe I buy more supplies here and there, but nothing I’d call crazy.
During those pumped-up periods, do you find yourself talking a lot more than usual?
I’m not sure. Maybe a little, if I’m excited about something, but I haven’t really noticed myself talking nonstop or anything.
During these pumped-up periods, has your behavior caused serious problems at work or at home?

Yeah… it’s caused problems. Work’s gotten messier than I want to admit—clients complaining about missed details, scheduling mix-ups. Even my apprentices kind of second-guess me now.

And at home… yeah, my wife and I argue a lot more. Mostly about the mortgage and the business. She thinks I’m risking everything we’ve built.
During these pumped-up periods, have you had thoughts or perceptions that other people said weren’t real?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I get intense about stuff, but I haven’t, like, seen things or believed something that people said wasn’t real. Not that I can think of.
Before these past few months, have you had other separate times in your life when you felt this same kind of pumped-up energy with much less need for sleep?
I don’t really know. Nothing this clear comes to mind… maybe I’ve had stretches where I was more keyed up, but I couldn’t say for sure it was the same thing.
How long has this stretch of sleeping only three or four hours and feeling pumped up been going on?
I guess… about seven months. It kind of started building after we took on the mortgage for the workshop and equipment.
Since this started, have you been drinking more alcohol than usual?
Not really sure. I mean… I’ve had drinks here and there, but I haven’t really been keeping track or thinking of it that way.
During this period, have you been getting a lot more done or starting a lot more work projects than you usually do?

Yeah… I mean, I’ve been keeping pretty busy. Going from job sites to bids, then back to the workshop messing with test panels. I’ve started a few home-automation ideas before finishing the last ones. Sitting still just feels… kind of like wasting time.
Between these pumped-up months, have you had times when your energy and sleep went back to your usual normal?
Not really, no. It’s been kind of… ongoing, I guess. Since we took on the mortgage for the workshop and equipment, about seven months ago, it’s just been building.
During this period, have you felt more confident or capable than usual?

Yeah… maybe. I’ve been feeling like I could take on bigger commercial jobs, even train a whole crew, like right now. I know on some level my license and experience aren’t exactly there for all of it, but it still feels like I could handle it.
Since this started, have you been using alcohol heavily?
No… not heavily. I’ll have a drink here and there, but I wouldn’t say it’s been a big thing.
Before these past seven months, was there a time when sleeping three or four hours a night would have felt normal for you?

No… before this, that wouldn’t have been normal for me. Lately it’s been more like three or four hours and then I’m just up before dawn, feeling ready to start pricing materials or checking emails like I slept fine.
Have these past several months ever led to you being unable to work at all for a period of time?

Not completely unable to work, no. I’ve still been showing up. But… it’s been getting messy. Clients have complained about details I missed, schedules getting mixed up. My apprentices don’t really trust my direction like they used to.

And at home it’s become a big issue. My wife and I keep arguing about the mortgage and the business… she thinks I’m risking everything we built.
Since this started, have you been using any stimulants, like cocaine, meth, or ADHD pills that weren’t prescribed to you?
No… I mean, not stuff like that. I haven’t been using cocaine or meth or taking pills that aren’t mine.
Since this started, have you been using a lot of caffeine or energy drinks?
Not really. I mean, I drink coffee sometimes, but I wouldn’t say it’s a lot or anything. No energy drinks, really.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a distinct 7-month period of persistently elevated/irritable mood and increased energy with markedly decreased need for sleep, increased goal-directed activity, inflated confidence, distractibility, and resulting occupational and marital impairment. Substance-induced causes were not supported by the interview, and the presentation is not well explained by ADHD or anxiety because symptoms are episodic/new compared with baseline and accompanied by classic manic-spectrum sleep and mood changes. Given clear bipolar-spectrum symptoms but incomplete lifetime history to subtype precisely, bipolar affective disorder unspecified is the best fit among the candidates.
